name: mandelbrot
axis: realistic whole program: f64 arithmetic in a tight escape loop + integer bit packing into an array row buffer
notes: Adapted from the Computer Language Benchmarks Game `mandelbrot` (50-iteration escape test, |Z|^2 > 4.0, bits packed 8 to a byte). ADAPTATION: the reference writes a binary PBM to stdout; all four here print a text summary of exactly the same bitmap — the in-set pixel count and a rolling checksum (checksum*31 + byte) mod 1000000007 kept in i64 — so stdout is comparable and no runtime has to reproduce another's integer-overflow rules. Every byte of the reference bitmap is still produced and consumed. Rust is scalar safe Rust (no SIMD intrinsics, no rayon); JS/Python are plain scalar loops (no numpy). Scale-verified: work is O(n^2), and n=4000 -> n=8000 gives rust 0.687->2.741s (3.99x), deno 0.762->3.012s (3.95x), VL 0.808->3.251s (4.02x), python n=400->1000 0.215->1.349s (6.27x vs the 6.25x expected). Python's N is 1000 (1/64 of the work). Final timings (min over all observations): rust 2.741s, deno 3.012s, VL 3.251s (prebuilt; 1.19x Rust, 1.08x deno), python(1000) 1.349s. `vl build -O3` 3.162s — a ~3% win.
